skill.name: parametric-scribe
skill.description: Records coding tasks in a recipe file so an agent can replay, revise, or fork earlier steps.
skill.summary: Track and replay coding history as editable recipe steps.
skill.author: Cycleaddict

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around filenames and YAML examples. One medium-risk item remains: the replay protocol instructs the agent to run git checkout against a recipe SHA, which can change repository state. I found no prompt injection text or data exfiltration intent in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Replay uses git checkout without guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, run git status first, and preserve uncommitted work before checkout.

remediation.issue: Recipe SHAs are trusted during replay.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that the target SHA exists in the local repository and came from the recipe before running commands.

content.user_title: Replay Coding History with Parametric Scribe
content.value_statement: Changing an early coding decision can make later edits hard to reuse. This skill records each task as a recipe step so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can replay and adapt history.
actual_capabilities: Records completed coding tasks as ordered recipe entries with intent, prompt, output files, and commit SHA.
Guides an agent to replay later steps after a user changes an earlier step.
Supports recipe variants for alternate implementation paths.
Keeps the recipe file as the source of truth for project history.
Provides a sample recipe format for teams adopting the workflow.
limitations: It relies on accurate recipe entries and commit SHAs.
It does not include scripts or automation to perform replay by itself.
Replay quality depends on the agent understanding changed project structure.
Git checkout steps can alter the working tree and require user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Revise an early architecture choice
use_cases.description: Change an initial framework choice and replay later implementation steps against the new foundation.

use_cases.title: Maintain reproducible coding sessions
use_cases.description: Record prompts, modified files, and commit references after each task for a clearer project timeline.

use_cases.title: Explore implementation variants
use_cases.description: Fork a recipe before a risky change so alternate solutions can be compared later.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Recipe
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Parametric Scribe while we build this feature. After each completed task, add a clear recipe entry with intent, files, and commit SHA.

prompt_templates.title: Record This Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the latest task to the recipe. Include the original prompt, the files changed, a short intent, and the current commit SHA.

prompt_templates.title: Replay From a Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Replay from step 003 using this new instruction: replace the Flask server with a FastAPI server. Adapt later steps to the current codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Compare a Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a variant of the recipe from step 004. Apply the new design direction there and keep the original recipe unchanged.

output_examples.input: Start tracking a new feature build.
output_examples.output: The skill would create a recipe-oriented workflow and remind the agent to record each completed task with intent, changed files, and commit reference.

output_examples.input: Change step 002 to use a different framework.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide the agent to return to the prior project state, apply the new instruction, then replay later intents in order.

output_examples.input: Create a variant before trying a new design.
output_examples.output: The skill would preserve the original recipe and describe a separate variant path for comparison.

best_practices: Commit or stash work before replaying a previous step.
Keep each recipe intent short, specific, and tied to user value.
Review adapted replay changes before accepting later steps.
anti_patterns: Do not run checkout commands without confirming the target SHA and working tree state.
Do not store secrets or private credentials in recipe prompts.
Do not treat replay as exact restoration when the project structure has changed.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI agent record coding tasks as recipe steps and replay them when earlier decisions change.

faq.question: Does it execute code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides instructions. Any command or edit still depends on the active AI tool and user approval.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can read skill instructions.

faq.question: Where is history stored?
faq.answer: The instructions use docs/recipe.yaml as the source of truth for recorded steps.

faq.question: Can it create project variants?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes copying the recipe to a variant file so alternate paths can be tracked separately.

faq.question: What should I check before replaying?
faq.answer: Confirm the target step, commit SHA, and working tree status before changing repository state.
